title: The four ways to put into a map
description:
Compare `operator[]`, `insert`, `insert_or_assign` and `try_emplace` by what their pages say they return and do.

```
operator[]("a") = 1          -> created
insert({"a", 2})             -> not inserted, value stays 1
insert_or_assign("a", 3)     -> assigned, value 3
try_emplace("b", 4)          -> inserted
try_emplace("b", 5)          -> not inserted, argument not used
```
hints: `insert` returns `std::pair<iterator, bool>`: the iterator points at the element that is there now, new or old (lesson 2.02).
`operator[]` needs a default-constructible value type; `Loud` is not, which is one more reason the other three exist.
requirements: Print the `bool` from each returned pair.
Use a value type that prints when it is constructed, to show when `try_emplace` does not build one.
Write one sentence for each saying when you would use it.
stretch: Look up the complexity of each and when "hint" overloads help.
